fdd5aa36b0.q: Why does the United States healthcare system cost significantly more than other developed nations despite being 3% of the world population?
fdd5aa36b0.a: The United States has the only free enterprise healthcare system on earth where prices are not controlled and hospitals and doctors are not employees or owned by the state. Almost all medical innovation on earth is designed for the American market because innovators make the bulk of their money selling to Americans. As a result, the quality of healthcare everywhere else on earth depends on the United States, which drives 40% of world healthcare spend.
fdd5aa36b0.e: Healthcare Fixed: No Insurance Needed, Same Doctors, 60% Less - David Goldhill

e1df1adce2.q: How does third-party payment insurance structure distort competition and pricing in healthcare markets?
e1df1adce2.a: Third-party payers determine how much providers can charge and how many customers they have, which removes incentive for competition. Unlike any other business, nobody in the healthcare system can make more money or be more profitable by lowering their prices. This keeps price levels artificially high and prevents the kind of competitive pricing seen in other industries like retail.
e1df1adce2.e: Healthcare Fixed: No Insurance Needed, Same Doctors, 60% Less - David Goldhill

fc9613d4b9.q: What is the lifetime cost burden for an average American employee and their family participating in the healthcare system?
fc9613d4b9.a: In 2012, when looking at what an employee would put into the healthcare system over her lifetime including employee premiums, employer premiums, Medicare taxes, and out-of-pocket costs, assuming she did not get really sick and had a couple of kids and a non-working partner, the total was 1.2 million dollars over a lifetime.
fc9613d4b9.e: Healthcare Fixed: No Insurance Needed, Same Doctors, 60% Less - David Goldhill

8a612e238c.q: How much of healthcare spending goes directly to administrative costs of the payment system rather than actual medical care?
8a612e238c.a: Administrative costs for the payment system account for somewhere between 10% and 15% directly of the cost of care. This translates to several thousand dollars a year per person, and over 80 years of life, consumers pay hundreds of thousands of dollars just for the operations of the third-party payment system.
8a612e238c.e: Healthcare Fixed: No Insurance Needed, Same Doctors, 60% Less - David Goldhill

2e7a4f9849.q: What is the actual cost of innovation in pharmaceutical development and how does competition affect pricing once drugs are established?
2e7a4f9849.a: The first pill to get approval costs $9 million because it requires all the research, studies, and regulatory testing. The second pill costs a penny to produce. When insurers do not cover drugs, prices come down through direct consumer competition, as seen with GLP-1 weight loss drugs where prices declined in the last three years without insurance coverage.
2e7a4f9849.e: Healthcare Fixed: No Insurance Needed, Same Doctors, 60% Less - David Goldhill

df11809354.q: How does Sesame create price transparency and competition in healthcare services compared to insurer-negotiated rates?
df11809354.a: Sesame lists consultations, appointments, procedures, labs, and diagnostics at cash prices set by physicians, clinics, or hospitals directly on its marketplace. Those prices are much lower than the prices that insurers pay because providers want to attract patients through competitive pricing, bringing normal market capitalism to healthcare.
df11809354.e: Healthcare Fixed: No Insurance Needed, Same Doctors, 60% Less - David Goldhill

9b163d9183.q: What is the potential impact of artificial intelligence on healthcare access and medical practice according to healthcare innovation leaders?
9b163d9183.a: AI could meaningfully improve diagnostic results, how doctors practice, how patient records are kept, and the ability to treat various conditions. An AI-driven vision could result in declining costs, improved data, and better outcomes with more personalized new drugs and treatments. However, to date, the biggest impact of AI in healthcare has been in revenue management and negotiation between providers and insurers rather than in clinical improvements.
9b163d9183.e: Healthcare Fixed: No Insurance Needed, Same Doctors, 60% Less - David Goldhill

65f8e4abd9.q: What are the three main financial myths that Garrett Gunderson identifies in his book Sacred Cows?
65f8e4abd9.a: The three main myths are: first, that it takes money to make money, when actually it takes relationships and ideas; second, that high risk equals high return, when wealthy people are actually good at mitigating and managing risk; and third, that you're in it for the long haul, which is a slow and dangerous way to run finances compared to focusing on cash flow and financial independence.
65f8e4abd9.e: The Daily Habits Behind Endless Income - Garrett Gunderson

d0305684e9.q: How should investors structure their portfolio based on investor DNA instead of premature diversification?
d0305684e9.a: Instead of diversifying prematurely, focus on investor DNA by first investing in yourself to gain skills and financial intelligence before saving another dollar. Then focus on financial independence through cash flow to cover lifestyle expenses. Plug financial leaks like taxes, interest, hidden fees, and improper insurance design. Finally, focus on velocity and three-dimensional assets that create equity, cash flow, and tax advantages rather than one-dimensional retirement plans.
d0305684e9.e: The Daily Habits Behind Endless Income - Garrett Gunderson

c25f64cbe0.q: What is the difference between capital and cash flow in wealth building, according to billionaire-level thinking?
c25f64cbe0.a: Billionaires talk about cash flow, not capital. They ask: what can I buy immediately that will either stop me from tipping the government or create more cash flow? This is a completely different conversation than asking how to accumulate a million or ten million dollars in the bank, which indicates lower financial literacy.
c25f64cbe0.e: The Daily Habits Behind Endless Income - Garrett Gunderson

d5883d3ff0.q: What asset classes does Garrett Gunderson focus on personally instead of index funds and broad diversification?
d5883d3ff0.a: Gunderson focuses primarily on his business to create enterprise value and cash flow, and has simplified his personal portfolio to include only one or two asset classes: gold, silver, and Bitcoin as hedges, plus some rental property he can drive to. He avoids index funds because most stock market companies he doesn't care about supporting, and prefers investments he can influence.
d5883d3ff0.e: The Daily Habits Behind Endless Income - Garrett Gunderson

78bd1bd182.q: What principle did Garrett Gunderson learn from Melvin Simon about investment selection?
78bd1bd182.a: Melvin Simon, the 64th richest person on the planet at the time, told Gunderson: don't invest in things you don't understand, period, full stop. This principle led Gunderson to avoid cryptocurrency despite being there when Bitcoin was a hundred dollars a coin, because he still doesn't fully understand blockchain technology.
78bd1bd182.e: The Daily Habits Behind Endless Income - Garrett Gunderson

7730474233.q: How should someone begin investing in themselves if they lack capital, according to Garrett Gunderson's daily framework?
7730474233.a: Start your day investing in yourself in three ways: exercise, education, and enlightenment. Take time to read books, listen to audio content, and ask yourself what one thing you could do to improve your life. Invest in specialized knowledge relevant to your goals, hire coaches and mentors who ask questions you don't ask yourself, create systems and rituals to reinforce learning, and build accountability through paid programs.
7730474233.e: The Daily Habits Behind Endless Income - Garrett Gunderson
